terms.guide_text: Number of business days until the start of the average OIS.
terms.name: SpotLag

terms.guide_text: The frequency of payments on the fixed leg.
terms.name: FixedTenor

terms.guide_text: The day count basis on the fixed leg.
terms.name: FixedDayCounter

terms.guide_text: The business day calendar on the fixed leg.
terms.name: FixedCalendar

terms.guide_text: The roll convention for accruals on the fixed leg.
terms.name: FixedConvention

terms.guide_text: The roll convention for payments on the fixed leg.
terms.name: FixedPaymentConvention

terms.guide_text: The frequency of payments on the fixed leg.
terms.name: FixedFrequency

terms.guide_text: The name of the overnight index.
terms.name: Index

terms.guide_text: The frequency of payments on the overnight leg.
terms.name: OnTenor

terms.guide_text: The rate cut-off on the overnight leg. Generally, the overnight fixing is only observed up to a certain number of days before the payment date and the last observed rate is applied for the remaining days in the period. This rate cut-off gives the number of days e.g.\ 2 for Fed Funds average OIS.
terms.name: RateCutoff

terms.guide_text: The name of an ibor, term rate or overnight index, e.g. USD-LIBOR-3M, USD-SOFR-3M, USD-SOFR
terms.name: Index

terms.guide_text: The name of a BMA / SIFMA index, e.g. USD-SIFMA
terms.name: BMAIndex

terms.guide_text: The payment calendar of the reference leg. If not specified, defaults to index fixing calendar.
terms.name: IndexPaymentCalendar

terms.guide_text: The payment convention of the reference leg. If not specified, defaults to Following.
terms.name: IndexPaymentConvention

terms.guide_text: The payment lag of the reference leg. If not specified, defaults to 0.
terms.name: IndexPaymentLag

terms.guide_text: The settlement days of the reference leg. If not specified, defaults to bma index fixing days.
terms.name: IndexSettlementDays

terms.guide_text: The payment period of the reference leg. If not specified, defaults to bma index tenor if reference index is overnight, otherwise to reference index tenor.
terms.name: IndexPaymentPeriod

terms.guide_text: The constant maturity index index name. This must be of the form "CMB-FAMILY-TENOR" where FAMILY can consist of any number of tags separated by "-"
terms.name: Id

terms.guide_text: Compounding of the yield - Simple, Compounded, Continuous, SimpleThenCompounded
terms.name: Compounding

terms.guide_text: Frequency of the cash flows - Annual, Semiannual, Quarterly, Monthly etc.
terms.name: Frequency

terms.guide_text: Dirty or Clean
terms.name: PriceType

terms.guide_text: The identifier for the CDS convention.
terms.name: Id

terms.guide_text: A boolean value indicating if an accrued fee is due on the occurrence of a credit event. Allowable boolean values are given in the Table the guide. In general, this is set true.
terms.name: SettlesAccrual

terms.guide_text: A boolean value indicating if the accrued fee, on the occurrence of a credit event, is payable at the credit event date or the end of the fee period. A value of true indicates that the accrued is payable at the credit event date and a value of false indicates that it is payable at the end of the fee period. In general, this is set true.
terms.name: PaysAtDefaultTime

terms.guide_text: The number of days after the CDS trade date when protection starts i.e.\ the Protection effective date or step-in date. Any non-negative integer is allowed here. For standard CDS after, this is generally set to 1.
terms.name: SettlementDays

terms.guide_text: The calendar associated with the CDS. For non-JPY currencies, this is generally WeekendsOnly to agree with the ISDA standard. For JPY CDS, the ISDA standard calendar is TYO documented at \url{https://www.cdsmodel.com/cdsmodel}. This could be set up as an additional calendar or JPN could be used as a proxy. Allowable calendar values are given in Table the guide.
terms.name: Calendar

terms.guide_text: The frequency of fee leg payments for the CDS. The ISDA standard is Quarterly but any valid frequency is allowed.
terms.name: Frequency

terms.guide_text: The business day convention for payments on the CDS. The ISDA standard is Following but any valid business day convention from Table the guide is allowed.
terms.name: PaymentConvention

terms.guide_text: The date generation rule for the fee leg on the CDS. The ISDA standard is CDS2015 but any valid date generation rule is allowed.
terms.name: Rule

terms.guide_text: The day counter for fee leg payments on the CDS. The ISDA standard is A360 but any valid day counter from Table the guide is allowed.
terms.name: DayCounter

terms.guide_text: The day counter for the last fee leg payment on the CDS. The ISDA standard is A360 (Incl Last) but any valid day counter from Table the guide is allowed. If not given, the following fallback rule applies: If DayCounter is A360, LastPeriodDayCounter is set to A360 (Incl Last), otherwise LastPeriodDayCounter is set to the same value as DayCounter.
terms.name: LastPeriodDayCounter

terms.guide_text: The calendar for the fixed rate leg of the swap.
terms.name: ForwardStart

terms.guide_text: The number of business days to spot for the CMS Spread Index.
terms.name: SpotDays

terms.guide_text: The frequency of payments on the CMS Spread leg.
terms.name: SwapTenor

terms.guide_text: The number of fixing days.
terms.name: FixingDays

terms.guide_text: The calendar for the CMS Spread leg.
terms.name: Calendar

terms.guide_text: The day counter for the CMS Spread leg.
terms.name: DayCounter

terms.guide_text: The rolling convention for the CMS Spread Leg.
terms.name: RollConvention

terms.guide_text: The identifier for the commodity forward convention. The identifier here should match the Name that would be provided for the commodity in the trade XML as described in Table the guide.
terms.name: Id

terms.guide_text: The number of business days to spot for the commodity. Any non-negative integer is allowed here. If omitted, this takes a default value of 2.
terms.name: SpotDays

terms.guide_text: This is only used if Outright is false. Any positive real number is allowed here. When Outright is false, the commodity forward quotes are provided as points i.e. a number that should be added to the commodity spot to give the outright commodity forward rate. The PointsFactor is the number by which the points quote should be divided before adding it to the spot quote to obtain the forward price. If omitted, this takes a default value of 1.
terms.name: PointsFactor

terms.guide_text: The business day calendar(s) used for advancing dates for both spot and forwards. The allowable values are given in Table the guide. If omitted, it defaults to NullCalendar i.e. a calendar where all days are considered good business days.
terms.name: AdvanceCalendar

terms.guide_text: The allowable values are true and false. If true, the forward tenor is interpreted as being relative to the spot date. If false, the forward tenor is interpreted as being relative to the valuation date. If omitted, it defaults to True.
terms.name: SpotRelative

terms.guide_text: Delivery location or delivery basis identifier for the commodity contract (for example, XCEC, XLME, PM). When provided, this value is used by FRTB commodity delta CRIF generation as Label2.
terms.name: DeliveryLocation

terms.guide_text: The business day roll convention used to adjust dates when getting from the valuation date to the spot date and the forward maturity date. The allowable values are given in Table the guide. If omitted, it defaults to Following.
terms.name: BusinessDayConvention

terms.guide_text: The allowable values are true and false. If true, the forward quotes are interpreted as outright forward prices. If false, the forward quotes are interpreted as points i.e. as a number that must be added to the spot price to get the outright forward price. If omitted, it defaults to true.
terms.name: Outright

terms.guide_text: The identifier for the commodity future convention. The identifier here should match the Name that would be provided for the commodity in the trade XML as described in Table the guide.
terms.name: Id

terms.guide_text: This node indicates the frequency of the commodity future contracts. The value here is usually Monthly or Quarterly, but allowed values are Daily, Weekly, Monthly, Quaterly and Annual.
terms.name: ContractFrequency

terms.guide_text: This node indicates the frequency of the commodity future options if it differs from the frequency of the underlying future contract. The value here is usually Monthly
terms.name: OptionContractFrequency

terms.guide_text: The business day trading calendar(s) applicable for the commodity future contract.
terms.name: Calendar

terms.guide_text: The business day expiry calendar(s) applicable for the commodity future contract. This calendar is used when deriving expiry dates. If omitted, this defaults to the trading day calendar specified in the Calendar node.
terms.name: ExpiryCalendar

terms.guide_text: The allowable values are any integer. This value indicates the number of months from the month containing the expiry date to the contract month. If 0, the commodity future contract expiry date is in the contract month. If the value of ExpiryMonthLag is n > 0, the commodity future contract expires in the n-th month prior to the contract month. If the value of ExpiryMonthLag is n < 0, the commodity future contract expires in the n-th month after the contract month. The value of ExpiryMonthLag is generally 0, 1 or 2. For example, NYMEX:CL has an ExpiryMonthLag of 1 and ICE:B has an ExpiryMonthLag of 2. If omitted, it defaults to 0.
terms.name: ExpiryMonthLag

terms.guide_text: This node takes a calendar month in the form of the first three characters of the month with the first character capitalised. The month provided should be an arbitrary valid future contract month. It is used in cases where the ContractFrequency is not Monthly in order to determine the valid contract months. If omitted, it defaults to January.
terms.name: OneContractMonth

terms.guide_text: The number of business days that the expiry date is before the base date where the base date is implied by the AnchorDay node above. Any non-negative integer is allowed here. If omitted, this takes a default value of zero.
terms.name: OffsetDays

terms.guide_text: The business day roll convention used to adjust the expiry date. The allowable values are given in Table the guide. If omitted, it defaults to Preceding.
terms.name: BusinessDayConvention

terms.guide_text: The allowable values are true and false. If true, if the base date implied by the AnchorDay node above is not a good business day according to the calendar provided in the Calendar node, this date is adjusted before the offset specified in the OffsetDays is applied. If false, this adjustment does not happen. If omitted, it defaults to true.
terms.name: AdjustBeforeOffset

terms.guide_text: The allowable values are true and false. This node indicates if the future contract is based on the average commodity price of the contract period. If omitted, it defaults to false.
terms.name: IsAveraging

terms.guide_text: The allowable values are any integer. This value indicates the number of months from the month containing the option expiry date to the month containing the expiry date. If 0, the commodity future option contract expiry date is anchored in the same month as the commodity future contract expiry date. If the value of OptionExpiryMonthLag is n > 0, the commodity option future contract expires in the n-th month prior to the commodity future contract expiry month. If the value of OptionExpiryMonthLag is n < 0, the commodity option future contract expires in the n-th month after the commodity future contract expiry month. The value of OptionExpiryMonthLag should be equal to ExpiryMonthLag when OptionExpiryOffset is used. The OptionExpiryMonthLag is rarely used. An example is the Crude Palm Oil contract XKLS:FCPO where the future contract expiry is in the delivery month and the option expiry is in the month that is 2 months prior to this. In this case, OptionExpiryMonthLag is 2. If omitted, OptionExpiryMonthLag defaults to 0.
terms.name: OptionExpiryMonthLag

terms.guide_text: This node can contain any non-negative integer. The option expiry date is this at least this number of business days before the contract expiry. The option expiry date is calculated using the regular rule and if the option expiry date falls on a date before this minimum date, the minimum date will be taken instead.
terms.name: OptionMinBusinessDaysBefore

terms.guide_text: The business day convention used to adjust the option expiry date to a good business day if OptionExpiryDay is used.
terms.name: OptionBusinessDayConvention

terms.guide_text: When building future curves, we may use market data that has a continuation expiry, i.e. c1, c2, etc. , as opposed to an explicit expiry date or tenor. In some cases, the continuation expiries coming from the market data provider may skip serial months and therefore we use the mapping here to map from the market data provider index to the relevant serial month.
terms.name: FutureContinuationMappings

terms.guide_text: When building option volatility structures, we may use market data that has a continuation expiry, i.e. c1, c2, etc. , as opposed to an explicit expiry date or tenor. In some cases, the continuation expiries coming from the market data provider may skip serial months and therefore we use the mapping here to map from the market data provider index to the relevant serial month. For example, for the Crude Palm Oil contract XKLS:FCPO, the option expiry months are serial up to the 9th month and then alternate months. So, we would add a mapping from 10 to 11, 11 to 13 and so on so that the correct option expiry is arrived at when reading the market data quotes and constructing the option volatility structure.
terms.name: OptionContinuationMappings

terms.guide_text: For power derivatives, quantities are sometimes given as a quantity per hour. To deduce the quantity for the day which is multiplied by that day's future price, one needs to know the number of hours in the day associated with the future price. For example ICE PDQ is the daily PJM Western Hub Real Time Peak future contract. The price each day for this contract is the average of the locational marginal prices (LMPs) for all hours ending 08:00 to 23:00 Eastern Pacific Time. In other words, there are 16 hours in the day that feed in to the average yielding this settlement price. For this contract, HoursPerDay would be 16. This field is only needed if a trade XML references this commodity contract, has CommodityQuantityFrequency set to PerHour and has no HoursPerDay value set directly in the XML.
terms.name: HoursPerDay

terms.guide_text: For some derivatives, quantities are given as quantity per calendar day and hour. The monthly quantity is then scaled by the number of calendar days times hours per day (see above) plus or minus a daylight savings correction. To compute the daylight savings correction a convention is needed that describes the dates on which dates one hour is gained resp. lost. Currently supported conventions are US, Null. Default is US if no convention is given.
terms.name: SavingsTime

terms.guide_text: Delivery location or delivery basis identifier for the commodity contract. When provided, this value is used by FRTB commodity delta CRIF generation as Label2 for commodity sensitivities. This can have a small impact on FRTB commodity capital via the commodity basis correlation term when two records have different delivery locations.
terms.name: DeliveryLocation

terms.guide_text: Sometimes the next contract expiry, as specified in the convention, is not the correct option underlying. For example the base metals options expiries on the 1st Wednesday of the contract month, and during the first 3 months there are daily future contracts available. The option underlying is not the future contract which matures on the option expiry but the one which matures on the 3rd Wednesday of the month. This field is referencing to an commodity future convention which specifies the correct expiry date for the underlying contract.
terms.name: OptionUnderlyingFutureConvention

terms.guide_text: The name of the commodity being averaged.
terms.name: CommodityName

terms.guide_text: This indicates the averaging period relative to the future expiry date. The allowable values are: \begin{itemize}
terms.name: Period

terms.guide_text: The pricing calendar(s) used to determine the pricing dates in the averaging period.
terms.name: PricingCalendar

terms.guide_text: A boolean flag that defaults to true if omitted. When set to true, the pricing dates in the averaging period are the set of PricingCalendar good business days. When set to false, the pricing dates in the averaging period are the complement of the set of PricingCalendar good business days. This may be useful in certain situations. For example, the contract ICE PW2 with specifications \href{https://www.theice.com/products/71090520/PJM-Western-Hub-Real-Time-Peak-2x16-Fixed-Price-Future}{here} averages the PJM Western Hub locational marginal prices over each day in the averaging period that is a Saturday, Sunday or NERC holiday. So, in this case, UseBusinessDays would be false and PricingCalendar would be US-NERC.
terms.name: UseBusinessDays

terms.guide_text: The identifier for the conventions associated with the commodity being averaged.
terms.name: Conventions

terms.guide_text: This node allows any non-negative integer value. When averaging a commodity future contract price over the averaging period, the averaging period may include an underlying future contract expiry date. This node's value indicates when we should begin using the next future contract's price in the averaging. If the value is zero, we should include the future contract prices up to and including the contract expiry. If the value is one, we should include the contract prices up to and including the day that is one business day before the contract expiry and then switch to using the next future contract's price thereafter. Similarly for other non-negative integer values. If this node is omitted, it is set to zero.
terms.name: DeliveryRollDays

terms.guide_text: This node allows any non-negative integer value. If this node is omitted, it is set to zero. This node indicates which future contract is being referenced on each Pricing Date in the averaging period by acting as an offset from the next available expiry date. If FutureMonthOffset is zero, the settlement price of the next available monthly contract that has not expired with respect to the Pricing Date is used as the price on that Pricing Date. If FutureMonthOffset is one, the settlement price of the second available monthly contract that has not expired with respect to the Pricing Date is used as the price on that Pricing Date. Similarly for other positive values of FutureMonthOffset.
terms.name: FutureMonthOffset

terms.guide_text: This node allows any non-negative integer value. It should only be used where the CommodityName being averaged has a daily contract frequency. If this node is omitted, it is set to zero. This node indicates which future contract is being referenced on each Pricing Date in the averaging period by acting as a business day offset, using the CommodityName's expiry calendar, from the Pricing Date. It is useful in the base metals market where the future contract being averaged on each Pricing Date is the cash contract on that Pricing Date i.e.\ the contract with expiry date two business days after the Pricing Date.
terms.name: DailyExpiryOffset

terms.guide_text: The number of business days to the start of the cross currency basis swap.
terms.name: SettlementDays

terms.guide_text: The business day calendar(s) for both legs and to arrive at the settlement date using the SettlementDays above.
terms.name: SettlementCalendar

terms.guide_text: The roll convention for both legs.
terms.name: RollConvention

terms.guide_text: The name of the index on the leg that does not have the cross currency basis spread.
terms.name: FlatIndex

terms.guide_text: The name of the index on the leg that has the cross currency basis spread.
terms.name: SpreadIndex

terms.guide_text: True if the end of month convention is to be used when generating the schedule on both legs, and False if not. If not provided, it defaults to False.
terms.name: EOM

terms.guide_text: True if the swap is mark-to-market resetting, and False otherwise. If not provided, it defaults to False.
terms.name: IsResettable

terms.guide_text: True if it is the notional on the leg paying the flat index that resets, and False otherwise. If not provided, it defaults to True.
terms.name: FlatIndexIsResettable

terms.guide_text: the flat leg period length (typical value is 3M), defaults to index tenor except for ON indices for which it defaults to 3M
terms.name: FlatTenor

terms.guide_text: the spread leg period length (typical value is 3M), defaults to index tenor except for ON indices for which it defaults to 3M
terms.name: SpreadTenor

terms.guide_text: the payment lag for the spread leg, allowable values are 0, 1, 2, ..., defaults to 0 if not given
terms.name: SpreadPaymentLag

terms.guide_text: the payment lag for the flat leg, allowable values are 0, 1, 2, ..., defaults to 0 if nove given
terms.name: FlatPaymentLag

terms.guide_text: Only relevant if spread leg is OIS, allowable values are true, false, defaults to false if not given
terms.name: SpreadIncludeSpread

terms.guide_text: Only relevant if spread leg is OIS, allowable values are 0D, 1D, ..., defaults to 0D if not given
terms.name: SpreadLookback

terms.guide_text: Only relevant if spread leg is OIS, allowable values are 0, 1, 2, ..., defaults to 0 if not given
terms.name: SpreadFixingDays

terms.guide_text: Only relevant if spread leg is OIS, allowable values are 0, 1, 2, ..., defaults to 0 if not given
terms.name: SpreadRateCutoff

terms.guide_text: Only relevant if spread leg is OIS, allowable values are true, false, defaults to false if not given
terms.name: SpreadIsAveraged

terms.guide_text: Only relevant if spread leg is OIS, allowable values are true, false, defaults to true if not given
terms.name: SpreadObservationShift

terms.guide_text: Only relevant if flat leg is OIS, allowable values are true, false, defaults to false if not given
terms.name: FlatIncludeSpread

terms.guide_text: Only relevant if flat leg is OIS, allowable values are 0D, 1D, ..., defaults to 0D if not given
terms.name: FlatLookback

terms.guide_text: Only relevant if flat leg is OIS, allowable values are 0, 1, 2, ..., defaults to 0 if not given
terms.name: FlatFixingDays

terms.guide_text: Only relevant if flat leg is OIS, allowable values are 0, 1, 2, ..., defaults to 0 if not given
terms.name: FlatRateCutoff

terms.guide_text: Only relevant if flat leg is OIS, allowable values are true, false, defaults to false if not given
terms.name: FlatIsAveraged

terms.guide_text: Only relevant if flat leg is OIS, allowable values are true, false, defaults to true if not given
terms.name: FlatObservationShift

terms.guide_text: The number of business days to the start of the cross currency basis swap.
terms.name: SettlementDays

terms.guide_text: The business day calendar(s) for both legs It is also used to arrive at the settlement date using the SettlementDays above.
terms.name: SettlementCalendar

terms.guide_text: The roll convention for both legs.
terms.name: SettlementConvention

terms.guide_text: The currency of the fixed leg.
terms.name: FixedCurrency

terms.guide_text: The frequency of the fixed leg payments.
terms.name: FixedFrequency

terms.guide_text: The business day roll convention for the fixed leg.
terms.name: FixedConvention

terms.guide_text: The day count convention for the fixed leg.
terms.name: FixedDayCounter

terms.guide_text: The name of the index on the floating leg.
terms.name: Index

terms.guide_text: true if the end of month convention is to be used when generating the schedule on both legs, and false if not. If not provided, it defaults to false.
terms.name: EOM

terms.guide_text: true if the swap is mark-to-market resetting, and false otherwise. If not provided, it defaults to false.
terms.name: IsResettable

terms.guide_text: If the swap is mark-to-market resetting, then this field indicates which leg's notional resets. It is true if it is the notional on the floating leg that resets, and false if it is the notional on the fixed leg that resets. If not provided, it defaults to true.
terms.name: FloatIndexIsResettable

terms.guide_text: If the leg is compounding, this field indicates whether or not to include the spread in the compounding. The allowable values are true or false. The default to false if not given.
terms.name: IncludeSpread

terms.guide_text: The lookback period for the overnight indexed leg. If provided, it must be a period that is a non-negative number of days. The allowable values are 0D, 1D etc. It defaults to 0D if not given.
terms.name: Lookback

terms.guide_text: The fixing lag to be used for the overnight index. If provided, it must be a non-negative integer. If not provided, the natural fixing lag of the overnight index is used.
terms.name: FixingDays

terms.guide_text: The number of rate cut-off days on the overnight leg. If provided, it must be a non-negative integer. If not provided, it defaults to 0 i.e. no rate cut-off.
terms.name: RateCutoff

terms.guide_text: This flag indicates whether the overnight leg is averaged or compounded. The allowable values are true or false. It defaults to false if not given, i.e. assumes a compounded overnight leg.
terms.name: IsAveraged

terms.guide_text: If a non-zero lookback is given, this flag indicates if the there is an observation shift or not. The allowable values are true or false. It defaults to true if not given.
terms.name: ObservationShift

terms.guide_text: True if the deposit conventions are index based and False if the conventions are given explicitly.
terms.name: IndexBased

terms.guide_text: The index family from which to imply the conventions for the deposit quote. For example, this could be EUR-EURIBOR, USD-LIBOR etc.
terms.name: Index

terms.guide_text: The business day calendar for the deposit quote.
terms.name: Calendar

terms.guide_text: The roll convention for the deposit quote.
terms.name: Convention

terms.guide_text: True if the end of month roll convention is to be used for the deposit quote and False if not.
terms.name: EOM

terms.guide_text: The day count basis associated with the deposit quote.
terms.name: DayCounter

terms.guide_text: The number of business days to spot for the currency pair.
terms.name: SpotDays

terms.guide_text: The source currency of the currency pair. The FX quote is assumed to give the number of units of target currency per unit of source currency.
terms.name: SourceCurrency

terms.guide_text: The target currency of the currency pair.
terms.name: TargetCurrency

terms.guide_text: The number by which a points quote for the currency pair should be divided before adding it to the spot quote to obtain the forward rate.
terms.name: PointsFactor

terms.guide_text: The business day calendar(s) used for advancing dates for both spot and forwards. If not provided, it defaults to a calendar with no holidays.
terms.name: AdvanceCalendar

terms.guide_text: True if the forward tenor is to be interpreted as being relative to the spot date. False if the forward tenor is to be interpreted as being relative to the valuation date. If not provided, it defaults to True.
terms.name: SpotRelative

terms.guide_text: A flag indicating whether the end of month roll convention is to be used for FX forward quotes. If not provided, it defaults to False.
terms.name: EOM

terms.guide_text: The business day convention used when advancing dates. If not provided, it defaults to Following.
terms.name: Convention

terms.guide_text: The name of the convention.
terms.name: Id

terms.guide_text: The underlying index of the futures, this is either a MM (i.e. Ibor) index like e.g. EUR-EURIBOR-3M or an overnight index like e.g. USD-SOFR.
terms.name: Index

terms.guide_text: Only relevant for OI futures. Can be Compounding (which is also the default value if no value is given) or Averaging. For example, SOFR 3M futures are compounding while SOFR 1M futures are averaging the daily overnight fixings over the calculation period of the future.
terms.name: OvernightIndexFutureNettingType

terms.guide_text: Controls how the expiry (and for OI futures, the start) date is derived from the expiry month. Accepted values are listed below. If not given this field defaults to IMM. \begin{itemize}
terms.name: DateGenerationRule

terms.guide_text: Only applicable to overnight index futures with date generation rule FirstDayOfMonth. Overwrites the calendar used to adjust the start and end date of the future. Optional, if not given, the overnight index publishing calendar will be used to adjust the future start and end date.
terms.name: Calendar

terms.guide_text: This field is mandatory for par sensitivity calculation when using overnight index futures. Specifies the tenor for the future (e.g., 3M for SOFR futures). When specified, the tenor must match the tenor in the market data quotes during curve building, otherwise an error will be raised. For example, for SOFR 3M futures, this should be set to 3M. This field can be left blank if no par conversion is needed (i.e., for curve building only).
terms.name: OvernightIndexTenor

terms.guide_text: The FX convention for the currency pair (see the guide). Optional, if not given, the FX spot days default to 2 and the advance calendar defaults to source ccy + target ccy default calendars.
terms.name: FXConventionID

terms.guide_text: Convention of ATM option quote (Choices are AtmNull, AtmSpot, AtmFwd, AtmDeltaNeutral, AtmVegaMax, AtmGammaMax, AtmPutCall50).
terms.name: AtmType

terms.guide_text: Convention of Delta option quote (Choices are Spot, Fwd, PaSpot, PaFwd).
terms.name: DeltaType

terms.guide_text: If given, different ATM and Delta conventions will be used if the option tenor is greater or equal the switch tenor ("long term" atm and delta type)
terms.name: SwitchTenor

terms.guide_text: Call (default), Put. Only relevant for BF, RR market data input.
terms.name: RiskReversalInFavorOf

terms.guide_text: Broker (default), Smile. Only relevant for BF, RR market data input.
terms.name: ButterflyStyle

terms.guide_text: The index name. This must be of the form "CCY-NAME-TENOR" with a currency "CCY", an index name "NAME" and a string "TENOR" representing a period. The name should not be "GENERIC", since this is reserved.
terms.name: Id

terms.guide_text: The fixing calendar of the index.
terms.name: FixingCalendar

terms.guide_text: The day count convention used by the index.
terms.name: DayCounter

terms.guide_text: The settlement days for the index. This must be a non-negative whole number.
terms.name: SettlementDays

terms.guide_text: The business day convention used by the index.
terms.name: BusinessDayConvention

terms.guide_text: A flag indicating whether the index employs the end of month convention.
terms.name: EndOfMonth

terms.guide_text: The calendar for the fixed rate leg of the swap.
terms.name: FixCalendar

terms.guide_text: The rolling convention for the fixed rate leg of the swap.
terms.name: FixConvention

terms.guide_text: The payoff or coupon day counter, applied to both legs.
terms.name: DayCounter

terms.guide_text: The underlying inflation index.
terms.name: Index

terms.name: InflationConvention

terms.name: StartDelayConvention

terms.guide_text: This is an optional node taking the values None, OnPublicationDate or AfterPublicationDate. If omitted, the value None is used. Currently, our only known use case for a value other than None is for Australian zero coupon inflation indexed swaps (ZCIIS). Here, the index is published quarterly on the last Wednesday of the month following the end of the reference quarter. The start date and maturity date of the market quoted ZCIIS roll to the next quarterly date after the publication date of the index. For example, the AU CPI value for Q3 2020, i.e.\ 1 Jul 2020 to 30 Sep 2020 was released on 28 Oct 2020. On 27 Oct 2020, before the index publication date, the market 5Y ZCIIS would start on 15 Sep 2020 and end on 15 Sep 2025 and reference the Q2 inflation index value. On 29 Oct 2020, after the index publication date, the market 5Y ZCIIS would start on 15 Dec 2020 and end on 15 Dec 2025 and reference the Q3 inflation index value. On the release date, i.e. 28 Oct 2020, the market ZCIIS that is set up is determined by whether the PublicationRoll value is OnPublicationDate or AfterPublicationDate. If it is set to OnPublicationDate, the swap rolls on this date and hence the market 5Y ZCIIS would start on 15 Dec 2020 and end on 15 Dec 2025 and reference the Q3 inflation index value. If it is set to AfterPublicationDate, the swap does not roll on the publication date and instead rolls on the next day, and hence the market 5Y ZCIIS would start on 15 Sep 2020 and end on 15 Sep 2025 and reference the Q2 inflation index value. The publication schedule for the index must be provided in the PublicationSchedule node if PublicationRoll is not None. An example of the AU CPI conventions set up is given in Listing the guide.
terms.name: PublicationRoll

terms.guide_text: The number of business days until the start of the OIS.
terms.name: SpotLag

terms.guide_text: The name of the overnight index. For example, this could be EUR-EONIA, USD-FedFunds etc.
terms.name: Index

terms.guide_text: The day count basis on the fixed leg of the OIS.
terms.name: FixedDayCounter

terms.guide_text: The business day calendar on the fixed leg. Optional to retain backwards compatibility with older versions, if not given defaults to index fixing calendar.
terms.name: FixedCalendar

terms.guide_text: The payment lag, as a number of business days, on both legs. If not provided, this defaults to 0.
terms.name: PaymentLag

terms.guide_text: True if the end of month roll convention is to be used when generating the OIS schedule and False if not. If not provided, this defaults to False.
terms.name: EOM

terms.guide_text: The frequency of payments on the fixed leg. If not provided, this defaults to Annual.
terms.name: FixedFrequency

terms.guide_text: The roll convention for accruals on the fixed leg. If not provided, this defaults to Following.
terms.name: FixedConvention

terms.guide_text: The roll convention for payments on the fixed leg. If not provided, this defaults to Following.
terms.name: FixedPaymentConvention

terms.guide_text: The rule used for generating the OIS dates schedule i.e.\ Backward or Forward. If not provided, this defaults to Backward.
terms.name: Rule

terms.guide_text: The business day calendar used for determining coupon payment dates. If not specified, this defaults to the fixing calendar defined on the overnight index.
terms.name: PaymentCalendar

terms.guide_text: The rate cut-off on the overnight leg. Generally, the overnight fixing is only observed up to a certain number of days before the end of the interest period date. The last observed rate is applied for the remaining days in the period. This rate cut-off gives the number of days e.g.\ 1 for ESTR or SOFR. If not specified, this defaults to 0 days.
terms.name: RateCutoff

terms.guide_text: The index name. This must be of the form "CCY-NAME" with a currency "CCY" and an index name "NAME". The name should not be "GENERIC", since this is reserved.
terms.name: Id

terms.guide_text: The fixing calendar of the index.
terms.name: FixingCalendar

terms.guide_text: The day count convention used by the index.
terms.name: DayCounter

terms.guide_text: The settlement days for the index. This must be a non-negative whole number.
terms.name: SettlementDays

terms.guide_text: The frequency of payments on the fixed leg.
terms.name: FixedFrequency

terms.guide_text: The day count basis on the fixed leg.
terms.name: FixedDayCounter

terms.guide_text: The Ibor index on the floating leg.
terms.name: Index

terms.guide_text: The business day calendar on the fixed leg.
terms.name: FixedCalendar

terms.guide_text: The roll convention on the fixed leg.
terms.name: FixedConvention

terms.guide_text: The frequency of payments on the floating leg, to be used if the frequency is different to the tenor of the index (e.g. CAD swaps for BA-3M have a 6M or 1Y payment frequency with a Compounding coupon)
terms.name: FloatFrequency

terms.guide_text: Defines how coupon rates should be calculated when the float frequency is different to that of the index. Possible values are "Compounding" and "Averaging".
terms.name: SubPeriodsCouponType

terms.guide_text: The index name. This must be of the form "CCY-CMS-TENOR" with a currency "CCY" and a string "TENOR" representing a period. The index name can contain an optional tag "CCY-CMS-TAG-TENOR" which is an arbitrary label that allows to define more than one swap index per currency.
terms.name: Id

terms.guide_text: A swap convention defining the index conventions.
terms.name: Conventions

terms.guide_text: The fixing calendar for the swap index fixings publication. If not given, the fixed leg calendar from the swap conventions will be used as a fall back.
terms.name: FixingCalendar

terms.guide_text: The name of Ibor/Overnight Index of the pay leg.
terms.name: PayIndex

terms.guide_text: The name of Ibor/Overnight Index of the receive leg.
terms.name: ReceiveIndex

terms.guide_text: The frequency of payments on the ReceiveIndex leg. This is usually the same as the ReceiveIndex's tenor. However, it can also be longer, e.g. overnight indexed vs overnight indexed basis swaps that may be quarterly on both legs. If not provided, this defaults to the ReceiveIndex's tenor.
terms.name: ReceiveFrequency

terms.guide_text: The frequency of payments on the PayIndex leg. This is usually the same as the PayIndex's tenor. However, it can also be longer, e.g. overnight indexed vs overnight indexed basis swaps that may be quarterly on both legs. If not provided, this defaults to the PayIndex's tenor.
terms.name: PayFrequency

terms.guide_text: True if the tenor basis swap quote has the spread on the pay index leg and False if not. If not provided, this defaults to True.
terms.name: SpreadOnRec

terms.guide_text: True if the tenor basis swap spread is to be included when compounding is performed on the spread leg and False if not. If not provided, this defaults to False.
terms.name: IncludeSpread

terms.guide_text: This field can have the value Compounding or Averaging. It applies to Ibor vs OI and Ibor vs Ibor basis swaps when the frequency of payments on the spread leg does not equal the spread leg index’s tenor. If Compounding is specified, then the spread tenor Ibor index is compounded and paid on the frequency specified in the corresponding node. If Averaging is specified, then the short tenor Ibor index is averaged and paid on the frequency specified in the corresponding node.
terms.name: SubPeriodsCouponType

terms.guide_text: True if the pay leg coupon is averaged and False if it is compounded.
terms.name: PayIsAveraged

terms.guide_text: True if the receive leg coupon is averaged and False if it is compounded.
terms.name: RecIsAveraged

terms.guide_text: The business day calendar on both swaps.
terms.name: Calendar

terms.guide_text: The frequency of payments on the fixed leg of the long swap.
terms.name: LongFixedFrequency

terms.guide_text: The roll convention on the fixed leg of the long swap.
terms.name: LongFixedConvention

terms.guide_text: The day count basis on the fixed leg of the long swap.
terms.name: LongFixedDayCounter

terms.guide_text: The Ibor index on the floating leg of the long swap.
terms.name: LongIndex

terms.guide_text: The frequency of payments on the fixed leg of the short swap.
terms.name: ShortFixedFrequency

terms.guide_text: The roll convention on the fixed leg of the short swap.
terms.name: ShortFixedConvention

terms.guide_text: The day count basis on the fixed leg of the short swap.
terms.name: ShortFixedDayCounter

terms.guide_text: The Ibor index on the floating leg of the short swap.
terms.name: ShortIndex

terms.guide_text: True if the basis swap spread is to be interpreted as the fair rate on the long swap minus the fair rate on the short swap and False if the basis swap spread is to be interpreted as the fair rate on the short swap minus the fair rate on the long swap. If not provided, it defaults to True.
terms.name: LongMinusShort

terms.guide_text: True if the conventions are for a tenor based zero quote and False if they are for a zero quote with an explicit maturity date.
terms.name: TenorBased

terms.guide_text: The day count basis associated with the zero rate quote (for choices see section the guide)
terms.name: DayCounter

terms.guide_text: The frequency of compounding (Choices are Once, Annual, Semiannual, Quarterly, Bimonthly, Monthly, Weekly, Daily).
terms.name: CompoundingFrequency

terms.guide_text: The type of compounding for the zero rate (Choices are Simple, Compounded, Continuous, SimpleThenCompounded).
terms.name: Compounding

terms.guide_text: The calendar used to advance from the spot date to the maturity date by the zero rate tenor (for choices see section the guide).
terms.name: TenorCalendar

terms.guide_text: The number of business days to advance from the valuation date before applying the zero rate tenor. If not provided, this defaults to 0.
terms.name: SpotLag

terms.guide_text: The calendar to use for business days when applying the SpotLag. If not provided, it defaults to a calendar with no holidays.
terms.name: SpotCalendar

terms.guide_text: The roll convention to use when applying the zero rate tenor. If not provided, it defaults to Following (Choices are Backward, Forward, Zero, ThirdWednesday, Twentieth, TwentiethIMM, CDS, ThirdThursday, ThirdFriday, MondayAfterThirdFriday, TuesdayAfterThirdFriday, LastWednesday).
terms.name: RollConvention

terms.guide_text: Whether or not to use the end of month convention when applying the zero rate tenor. If not provided, it defaults to false.
terms.name: EOM

terms.guide_text: The new inflation index name.
terms.name: Id

terms.guide_text: The name of the region with which the inflation index is associated.
terms.name: RegionName

terms.guide_text: A code for the region with which the inflation index is associated.
terms.name: RegionCode

terms.guide_text: A boolean flag indicating whether the index is a revised index or not. This is generally set to false but is left as an option to align with the C++ InflationIndex class definition.
terms.name: Revised

terms.guide_text: A valid frequency indicating the publication frequency of the inflation index, generally Monthly, Quarterly or Annual.
terms.name: Frequency

terms.guide_text: A valid period indicating the lag between the inflation index publication for a given period and the period itself. For example, if March's inflation index value is published in April, the AvailabilityLag would be 1M.
terms.name: AvailabilityLag

terms.guide_text: The ISO currency code of the currency associated with the inflation index, generally the currency of the region.
terms.name: Currency
